title: [v0.92.1][TAIL-06.10][security] Authenticate AWS and GCP mutation authorization
summary: Cloud mutation approval now requires an externally anchored operator signature; AWS additionally binds authenticated account identity, actual tfplan bytes, its digest sidecar, and a Terraform-derived reviewed projection.
integration_result: Implementation and local proof are tracked on codex/815-cloud-authorization-authenticity in the bound FastWork worktree; PR publication and merge are not yet claimed.
validation_result: The #815 no-cloud matrix passed for valid signed packets and rejected unsigned/forged approval, changed plan bytes, changed digest sidecar, changed JSON, Terraform projection drift, expiry, and cross-account/project replay. GCP provider-call preflight, AWS/GCP read-only availability, Python compilation, shell syntax, native six-card validation, and diff hygiene passed.
verification_scope: #727 AWS authorization validator and template/runbook; #731 GCP authorization validator and mutation preflight; shared #815 verifier, canonical signature contract, GCP template, and deterministic local fixtures.
validation_effect: Proves editable JSON and mutable digest sidecars cannot independently grant mutation authority, provider identity and exact plan bytes are bound, every required tamper/replay case fails before provider invocation, and read-only proof remains usable without approval.
notes_risks_inline: No paid cloud mutation ran. Production requires an operator-controlled Ed25519 private key and a non-group/world-writable allowed-signers file at $HOME/keys/adl-cloud-authorization.allowed_signers. Historical unsigned packets are not reusable authority.
